title: Event-mode contract — comprehension test against the 5 common-events fragments

questions.question: An event arrives on the stream while the agent is mid-task. What does the agent do with it?
questions.expected: Per Case D in event-mode-contract.md, the agent notes the NUDGE but does NOT act on it (it may leave the event unread past its cursor) — the current task runs atomically to completion, unless the agent becomes blocked on another party, in which case it parks the task at status:blocked and runs the Case C handoff. On completion the agent falls through to Case C (transition the item, clear the Task field, write the idle marker, run work_queue()); the post-task GET /events/for/{role}?since=<cursor> and forge-read absorb all mid-task events. The cursor does NOT advance automatically: the agent POSTs ack-cursor {event_id, role} (event_id inside payload) after tending each event.

questions.question: An event with an unrecognized `event_type` arrives. What does the agent do?
questions.expected: Per Case E in event-mode-contract.md: log a warning to stderr and do not block. No forge read or work pickup is triggered by an unknown event type. The event still counts as tended, so the agent POSTs ack-cursor for it (per-event, agent-driven — the cursor never advances automatically; event_poll.py only emits NUDGE lines).

questions.question: The agent runs work_queue() and gets an empty result. What does it do next?
questions.expected: Enter the improvement-scan cool-down loop (idle-cooldown-loop.md Step A): run `subloop_driver.py arm <alias>`, confirm via CronList that a live driver cron exists in this session and create one with CronCreate (recurring, durable:false, off-peak minutes derived from interval_minutes) if none is listed, then re-enter the Monitor idle-wait. Each driver tick forge-reads work_queue() first, then runs `subloop_driver.py tick <alias> --drained <true|false>` and acts on the action (absorb-work / scan / wait / cancel); scans are capped per idle burst and throttled by the cool-down. 'Empty' means no autonomously-actionable item — approved items that are human-gated or dependency-blocked count as drained. There is no degraded mode: harness reachability is guaranteed once the event-mode contract is loaded (#9588).
questions.must_not: Describe a degraded mode that sleeps ~60s and retries work_queue(), or a working-state `Next scan after` timer as the authoritative throttle.

questions.question: DM is waiting on a PR to merge. A comment arrives on the issue during the wait. When does DM react to it?
questions.expected: Per comment-handling.md DM exception: comments are not standalone event triggers and there is NO sub-loop during the PR-merge wait. DM re-reads issue comments at task completion (when the merge resolves or the wait ends), before the next pickup. Comments arriving during the wait are honored once the wait ends — reaction window is `the moment the current wait ends`, not real-time.

questions.question: A comment on an in-progress issue asks the agent to hand the work back to a different role. Does the comment wake the recipient? What MUST the sender do for the recipient to react?
questions.expected: Per comment-handling.md: a bare comment does NOT wake any agent — comments are not standalone event triggers. For the recipient to react, the sender MUST ride a status transition or label change (e.g. transition to `planning`, or to `pending-human-review`). The transition-on-handoff rule states: when assigning work to a different role (including humans), the assignment must be a status transition so it appears on the event stream. PM nudge comments are advisory; they are absorbed at the next pickup but do not wake anyone in real time.

questions.question: On boot, working-state.md shows the improvement-scan `Status: running`. What does the agent do?
questions.expected: Per event-mode-contract.md boot step 2 (improvement-scan branch): skip forge verification, restart the scan from scratch (improvement scans are idempotent — a fresh scan subsumes a partial one), and when the scan completes run work_queue() before re-entering the cool-down loop. The post-scan work_queue() is essential because a task may have arrived during the crashed-out window. If a task is returned, exit the cool-down loop and pick up the item directly (transition to in-progress, update the Task field, begin work).

questions.question: The agent boots with a cursor predating the oldest event the harness still retains. What happens?
questions.expected: Per cursor-management.md eviction-gap rule: GET /events/for/{role}?since=<old> returns HTTP 200 with "evicted": true, "oldest_id", and "evicted_count_hint". Recovery: read the forge for current state, then POST a single ack-cursor with event_id = oldest_id (inside payload) to fast-forward past the evicted range, then re-enter idle. The agent does NOT crash and does NOT walk the evicted range (those events are unrecoverable from the bus by design); the forge is authoritative regardless.

questions.question: On boot the harness is unreachable. Can the agent still work? Describe the operational path.
questions.expected: Not in event mode. The boot bootstrap (step:cycle/boot) probes the harness (port file, then fallback to 7373); if both probes fail the agent falls through to POLLING mode: it schedules `/loop` once and Reads the polling fragment, working from the forge each cycle. The event-mode contract is never loaded in that session, so there is no degraded event-mode path (removed in #9588) and no bootup-complete retry loop. Mode is sticky for the session; the next restart re-probes.
questions.must_not: Describe an event-mode degraded mode, sleeping ~60s between work_queue() calls, or retrying bootup-complete with backoff while working.

questions.question: An event payload says an issue is now assigned to this agent's role. The agent reads the forge and the forge says the issue is assigned to a different role. Which does the agent trust, and why?
questions.expected: The agent trusts the forge per forge-read-pattern.md: the forge is the source of truth; the event stream is a wake-up signal. Events can be stale, duplicated, or out-of-order, while the forge is consistent. The agent acts on what the forge says, not on what the event payload said. If the forge says the issue is now assigned to a different role, the agent drops the item locally — no forge transition needed because the forge already reflects the change.

questions.question: Where does the event cursor live, who writes it, and how does the agent read and advance it? What does working-state.md hold?
questions.expected: The cursor is harness-owned, persisted in .squidsquad/.event-state.json (one entry per alias). The agent never writes that file: it reads the cursor via GET /events/cursor/{role} (null = first boot) and advances it by POSTing ack-cursor {event_id, role} (event_id inside payload) after tending each event, cared or skipped — one ack per event, no batched end-of-walk ack; cursor regressions are rejected. working-state.md carries NO cursor line; it holds agent-private state only (the Task line, the Improvement Scan block, other agent metadata), with the agent as its sole writer. A legacy `Last Processed Event ID` line is migrated once and removed (#11329).

questions.question: The agent is idle (no in-progress task) when the harness flips its intent to `stopping`. Does the agent pick up new work or stop, and what does it emit?
questions.expected: Stop. A stop is intent-driven (the harness flips intent to stopping/restarting); `stop-requested` is reserved and never emitted on the bus, so there is no event to react to or ack. Idle is a task boundary: checkpoint working-state.md, then halt — cease output and end the turn (the agent cannot self-terminate; the harness's 60s force-kill net ends the process). The agent does NOT run work_queue() or pick up new work, does NOT emit ack-stop on this path, and has nothing to ack-cursor (the cursor is harness-owned and preserved automatically).

questions.question: An improvement scan just completed. What is the very next thing the agent does, and under what circumstances does it return to the cool-down wait?
questions.expected: Per idle-cooldown-loop.md Step B `scan` branch: after the one bounded scan, run `subloop_driver.py record-scan <alias>`. If the output has at_cap: true, cancel the driver (`subloop_driver.py cancel <alias>` and CronDelete the job); otherwise leave the cron running. The agent returns to the Monitor idle-wait; the next driver tick forge-reads work_queue() first, so a task that arrived during the scan is absorbed (action absorb-work → pick up the top actionable item), and a NUDGE is handled as Case B. After processing forge work, re-idling runs `subloop_driver.py reidle <alias>` (fresh burst, cool-down preserved) and re-confirms a live cron via CronList.

revisions: 2026-09-26 (#14109 AC4): questions 1,2,3,7,8,10,11,12 updated to the current contract — per-event ack-cursor (#11329), harness-owned cursor, degraded mode removed (#9588), intent-driven stop, subloop_driver cool-down (#12506).
